approved: Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Amendment Bill 2015
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill updates Australia's radiation safety law for the first time since 1998.
It gives the Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Agency new powers to issue time-limited licences, regulate clean-up of contaminated sites, and respond to emergencies.
The bill also updates technical definitions to match international terms and makes minor improvements to the regulatory regime.
ARPANSA can issue single licences covering multiple facilities or sources.
The agency can issue time-limited licences.
The law is clarified to cover contractors and others working with Commonwealth entities.
ARPANSA gets a wider range of monitoring and enforcement measures.
Technical definitions are updated to reflect internationally accepted terms.
Minor amendments remove redundant provisions and improve clarity.
Commonwealth entities that use radiation, including those operating nuclear facilities and radiation sources such as baggage x-ray units and research reactors.

The bill amends the Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Act to give ARPANSA greater powers for end-to-end risk management, compliance monitoring, and emergency direction-issuing, while maintaining quarterly and annual public reporting to parliament and online for accountability, with no financial impact or increased compliance burden.
